questions.question: A vector differs from a scalar because a vector requires:
options: Both a magnitude and a direction to be fully described

questions.question: The reliable test for classifying a quantity is to ask:
options: Is the quantity measured with a ruler?
Does a direction make sense and is it needed to complete the meaning?

questions.question: Why do vectors need different arithmetic from scalars?
options: Vectors are always larger than scalars
They do not — all quantities add identically
Vectors can partially or fully cancel depending on their directions

subtopics.title: Classifying the Five — and the Famous Pairs

questions.question: Which classification of the five quantities is correct?
options: Vectors: speed, energy; scalars: displacement, force, velocity
Vectors: displacement, force, velocity; scalars: speed, energy
Vectors: displacement only; scalars: the other four

questions.question: An athlete completes one full 400 m track lap. Distance and displacement are:
options: Distance 400 m; displacement zero — start and finish coincide

questions.question: For that same 80-second lap, average speed and average velocity are:
options: Speed 5 m/s; velocity zero, because displacement was zero

questions.question: Velocity is best described as:
options: Speed with its direction attached — the rate of change of position

subtopics.title: The Resultant — 30 N East Meets 50 N West

questions.question: With east chosen positive, 30 N east and 50 N west become:
The resultant of 30 N east and 50 N west is:
Why is '80 N' the classic wrong answer here?
options: It forgets to double the larger force
It adds the magnitudes with scalar arithmetic, ignoring that the forces oppose each other

questions.question: Which sanity checks confirm '20 N west'?
options: The resultant points with the larger force, and its size is the difference 50 N − 30 N
The resultant must equal the smaller force
No checks are possible for vectors

subtopics.title: The Toolkit, the Special Cases, and the Road to Matric

questions.question: The four-step method for adding vectors on a line is:
options: Add all magnitudes, then pick the most common direction
Draw a circle, measure angles, average them
Declare a positive direction; convert vectors to signed numbers; add algebraically; translate the sign back into a direction
Multiply the magnitudes and halve the result

questions.question: Forces of 50 N east and 50 N west act on an object. The resultant is:
In which single case does adding magnitudes directly give the correct resultant?
options: When all the vectors point in the same direction

questions.question: A final vector answer must always include:
options: Both the magnitude with units AND the direction
The sign convention written into the answer

questions.question: Which statement is complete on its own, needing no direction?
options: A push of 30 N on a bakkie
A trip of 3 km from home
A loaf of bread costs eighteen rand

questions.question: The 'sentence test' for energy — 'five hundred joules northward' — shows that energy is:
options: A vector, because it is powerful
A scalar, because the direction adds nothing to the meaning
A vector, because batteries have two terminals
Neither a vector nor a scalar

questions.question: A speed on a road sign becomes a velocity when:
options: It is measured in metres per second
It is written with a decimal comma
A direction of travel is attached to it

questions.question: You run once around a 400 m block and stop at your own gate. Your distance and displacement are:
Distance and displacement disagree because:
options: Displacement is measured in different units
Distance is always the larger number by definition
Distance asks how much moving happened; displacement asks what the moving achieved
One of them is always wrong

questions.question: That 400 m lap took 80 seconds. The average velocity is:
options: 0 m/s, because the displacement was zero

questions.question: Running the same 400 m straight up the road in 80 s instead would give:
options: Distance 400 m, displacement 400 m north, velocity 5 m/s north

questions.question: In the tug-of-war picture, why is the answer 20 N and not 80 N?
options: Because 30 N of the stronger team's pull is used up cancelling the weaker team, leaving 20 N spare

questions.question: 'Declare a positive direction' means:
options: Choose a direction, call it positive, and keep that choice to the final line
Use positive numbers only for large forces

questions.question: Forces of 30 N east and 50 N east act on the same crate. The resultant is:
Why is 'twenty newtons' only half an answer?
options: Because the number should be negative
Because forces are always written in kilonewtons
Because a vector answer needs its direction too — 20 N west
